children: A single Xos Hub™ has surpassed one gigawatt-hour of energy across more than 33,600 charging sessions in the field, field-proven performance that supports Xos's expansion across new products and markets
More than 1 gigawatt-hour (1,020,143.6 kWh) of energy delivered from a single, grid-independent Hub in demanding, real-world commercial operation
More than 33,600 charging sessions completed, charging vehicles day after day in continuous, real-world operation
That proven performance is already translating into growth, with recent orders from Xcel Energy and the U.S. Air Force.
The Xos Hub™, a mobile, grid-independent energy storage and charging system that delivers high-throughput commercial charging without permanent infrastructure or utility upgrades.
LOS ANGELES, Sept. 01, 2026
-- Xos, Inc.

(“Xos” or the “Company”), a leader in electric commercial vehicles and mobile charging solutions, today announced that a single Xos Hub™ has surpassed one gigawatt-hour (GWh) of cumulative energy delivered. The milestone provides multi-year field evidence of the Hub’s durability under continuous, real-world use, the same product strength that is helping Xos grow its energy storage business across new versions and markets.

Over the past year, the Company has expanded the Hub to higher capacity, launched the megawatt-scale Power Hub, deepened its utility deployments, and entered the defense market, and durability proven in the field is what makes that expansion credible. Across the deployed fleet, the Hub has operated in a wide range of climates and applications, from Northeast winters to Arizona summers, charging trucks, cars, buses, and autonomous vehicles for uses that span fleet operations and disaster response.

The Xos Hub is a mobile, grid-independent system, and a result like this measures what a specification sheet cannot: how the unit holds up delivering energy over years of continuous use, the pairing of sustained output and battery health that determines how a storage asset performs and what it costs to run over its service life.

"Reaching a gigawatt-hour from a single Hub gives us multi-year data on how this platform performs under continuous, real-world use. That track record is the foundation for how we are growing this business across new products and markets, and it shows customers across multiple industries why they can rely on it. We built the Hub to deliver energy every day, over years, and the field data now supports that,"
said Dakota Semler, Chief Executive Officer of Xos.
A Growing Energy Storage Business
Demand for energy storage and flexible charging is climbing. U.S. energy storage installations reached a record 18.9 gigawatts in 2025, up 52% from the prior year, according to

params.linkText: Wood Mackenzie and the American Clean Power Association.

children: At the same time, connecting new capacity to the grid remains a bottleneck: roughly 2,061 gigawatts of generation and storage are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues, and a typical project now takes more than five years to reach commercial operation,

params.linkText: according to Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.

children: The Xos Hub speaks directly to both trends as a deployable, grid-independent system that adds power without waiting on utility upgrades, and the durability behind this milestone is helping the Company broaden the platform to serve more of that demand:
Higher-capacity Hub versions:
In January 2026, Xos expanded Hub capacity tiers to up to 630 kWh per unit, widening the range of fleet and site applications the platform can serve.
Power Hub for large loads:
In June 2026, Xos introduced the Power Hub, a containerized system that scales the Hub architecture to megawatt-scale power for large loads, available in 1.2, 2.5, and 4.0 MWh configurations.
Utility deployments:
In August 2026, Xcel Energy placed a follow-on order for three Xos Hub systems in Colorado, supporting fleet EV charging at service centers and residential customers during grid upgrade construction.
Defense market entry:
In August 2026, Xos received a prototype Other Transaction Agreement from the U.S. Air Force to provide deployable mobile charging for electrified equipment and vehicles in field environments.
Safety certification:
In August 2026, the Xos Hub achieved UL 2202 certification for fleet energy storage systems.

"Field results at this scale strengthen the total cost of ownership case behind our customers' decisions, and that case only grows as our systems accumulate operating data. As we bring the next generation of higher-capacity Hubs and the Power Hub to market, we expect proven economic performance like this to accelerate adoption across fleet, utility, and industrial customers,"
said Giordano Sordoni, Chief Operating Officer of Xos.

This milestone is a proof point for a much larger trajectory. As commercial fleets, utilities, and energy-intensive operations move to electrify, the ability to deliver reliable charging and energy storage without permanent infrastructure is becoming central to how these customers plan and invest. Xos expects the field-validated durability behind this milestone to grow into a lasting competitive advantage, giving buyers measurable evidence rather than projections as they commit to electrification. Building on that foundation, the Company plans to scale the Hub platform into higher-capacity systems and large-scale power and to deepen its presence across fleet, utility, industrial, and defense markets in the years ahead.
About Xos
Xos, Inc.

is a leading manufacturer of fully electric commercial vehicles and mobile charging solutions, purpose-built for the demanding requirements of last-mile and return-to-base commercial fleet operations. The Company’s product portfolio includes the Xos Stepvan and Class 8 trucks, as well as Xos Hub™ mobile and stationary energy storage systems that enable fleet charging without costly infrastructure upgrades. Xos vehicles are designed and engineered to deliver lower total cost of ownership compared to conventional diesel vehicles, with zero direct emissions, lower maintenance costs, and improved operational efficiency. For more information, visit www.xostrucks.com.
